canvas-01-1.description: The bottom of Sheet 1, below the key map, index and the boxed station area, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north about 8 degrees anticlockwise of the page. It shows the western end of Main Street, running across the sheet, with Harrel Street and Canby Street (both marked arbitrary, for their house numbering) leaving it to the south. Frame dwellings with automobile sheds stand on both sides of Main Street, with an automobile repair shop with gasoline tanks on the north side. The Lebanon M.E. Church with its Sunday school stands at the upper right, east of a long shed, behind a heavy line marked no exposure that separates this part from the station area above. The lots are long and open behind the houses. The part has two street junctions, both on Main Street, and is placed by a two-point similarity fit through them.
notes: Harrel is now Nitzer Avenue and Canby is now Myrtle Avenue.
Placed by a two-point (helmert) fit on Main Street; the fitted scale is 5 percent larger than the scale bar, so positions away from Main Street between Harrel and Canby are less certain.

Printed sheet 1, 50 ft to an inch. Top: key, location map, key map of the borough (600 ft to an inch), index, water and fire notes: left out of the masks. Part 1: Main Street at Harrel (now Nitzer Avenue) and Canby (now Myrtle Avenue) Streets, M.E. church. Part 2: boxed station area with the C.R.R. of N.J., Excel Foundries, Station Place, Central Street, Knox Fence Co. and Cushetunk Mountain Creamery.

canvas-01-2.description: A boxed area in the middle of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own compass, north about 8 degrees anticlockwise of the page. It shows the Central Railroad of New Jersey main line crossing the box, with a siding, the railroad station south of the tracks and Station Place (marked arbitrary) running along them. North of the tracks are the Excel Foundries, with the foundry, core room, cleaning shop, machine shop and a concrete block storage building, and Central Street curving down to the tracks at the right. South of Station Place are dwellings, the Knox Fence Co. (not in operation) and the Cushetunk Mountain Creamery in concrete block buildings. The right side of the box is blank, and its lower edge is marked no exposure. The part was placed from one hand-picked point, the crossing of Central Street and the railroad, with the scale of the sheet and the direction of its compass.
notes: Station Place is probably today's Railroad Avenue, which meets Central Street at the crossing.
Placed from one hand-picked point (Central Street at the railroad) with rotation from the compass. Low confidence away from that point.

sheet-2.description: The western half of the centre of Lebanon on Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north about 9 degrees anticlockwise of the page. Main Street runs across the top of the sheet and Brunswick Avenue across the bottom; between them run High Street and Maple Street, and Cokesbury Road enters Main Street at the top right corner. The blocks are residential, with frame dwellings, automobile sheds and outbuildings on long lots. The Lebanon Public School stands in the middle of the block between High and Maple Streets. On Main Street are the post office and an automobile repair shop near Cokesbury Road and the Lebanon Hotel on the corner east of Maple Street. Two greenhouses with an office stand at the left edge of the sheet, west of High Street. The lots south of Brunswick Avenue are drawn along the bottom edge. The sheet continues east on Sheet 3 at Maple Street and Cokesbury Road.
notes: High Street / Main Street carries a residual of 3.7 m; the other four junctions 0.5 to 2.4 m.
Printed sheet 2, 50 ft to an inch, north about -9 degrees. Main Street, High Street, Maple Street, Brunswick Avenue, Cokesbury Road; Lebanon Public School, Lebanon Hotel, post office. One part.

sheet-3.description: The eastern half of the centre of Lebanon on Sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north about 8 degrees anticlockwise of the page. Main Street runs across the top from Cokesbury Road at the upper left, Cherry Street runs down the right side to Brunswick Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the sheet, and Central Street leaves Brunswick Avenue at the bottom left; Maple Street is just inside the left edge. The north side of Main Street has the Borough Hall and fire department, an automobile repair shop and dwellings; the south side has dwellings and a row of stores. Much of the large block between Main Street, Cherry Street and Brunswick Avenue is the cemetery, with the Reformed Dutch Church and its Sunday school near Brunswick Avenue and two long sheds behind them. Frame dwellings line Cherry Street on both sides and the south side of Brunswick Avenue. The sheet adjoins Sheet 2 to the west.
notes: Brunswick Avenue / Central Street carries a residual of 4.0 m and Brunswick Avenue / Cherry Street 3.2 m; only four junctions control the sheet.

Printed sheet 3, 50 ft to an inch, north about -8 degrees. Main Street, Cokesbury Road, Cherry Street, Brunswick Avenue, Central Street; Borough Hall and fire department, Reformed Dutch Church, cemetery. One part.
